title: Tiered invite-delegation for external collaborators and scoped invite operators
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Org admins frequently delegate ad-hoc invite duties to engineers or contractors which creates excessive blast radius (broad admin rights, unclear revocation, sparse audit metadata). We need a mechanism to allow limited invite delegation, scoped to teams and time windows, with enforced approval steps for external domains and enriched audit logs for post-incident reconstruction.

Goal: Implement a Tiered Invite Delegation feature that introduces: 
1) Invite Operator role: a constrained admin role that can send and revoke invitations but cannot change RBAC or billing. Operators have scoped team boundaries (single team, set of teams) and optional expiry. 
2) Approval chain for external domains: invites to domains not on the org allowlist require a two-step approval (Operator -> Team Admin -> Org Admin) or auto-block based on domain reputation thresholds. 
3) SAML attribute mapping hooks: honor sso:invite_scope claim when present to auto-assign invite scope and bypass certain approvals for enterprise-managed collaborators. 
4) Audit log enrichment: log invite metadata (inviter_id, operator_role_id, approval_chain, domain_reputation_score, expiration_ts) as structured entries to the audit store so Search/Playbooks can reliably reconstruct timelines.

Constraints: Changes must not expand current admin surface; must be compatible with RBAC v2 role model and SSO/SAML attribute mappings. Must include migration plan for existing delegated invite tokens and deprecation timeline for legacy invite keys.
comments: 2026-02-19 - Kickoff: scoped feature spec reviewed with PM and Design. Concern raised about UX friction for rapid contractor onboarding; agreed to add a temporary 'fast-track' path that records a mandatory audit justification and requires retroactive approval within 48h.

2026-02-25 - Security review (initial): recommended to store domain reputation score from external provider (Proofpoint) and use threshold config per org. Also flagged need for rate-limiting on operator invites to prevent bulk invite abuse.

2026-03-02 - Design review: added a compact operator management view in Console (operators list with scope, expiry, last-used timestamp, and revoke button). Mockups stored in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Tiered+Invite+Delegation

2026-03-05 - Engineering spike: implemented invite operator role in local RBAC v2 shim. Prototype stores operator_scope as CSV of team IDs and expiry_ts in invite_operator table. PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1289

2026-03-08 - Ops: integration test plan drafted to ensure audit logs include operator_role_id and approval_chain. Will push to staging along with SAML attribute mapping tests against Okta test tenant.

2026-03-10 - Blocker discovered: existing legacy invite tokens are issued without inviter metadata; migration strategy needed to annotate old tokens or rotate them. Decided on plan: expire tokens older than 90 days and email impacted users, and add server-side annotation where possible.

2026-03-12 - Next steps: finish API endpoints for operator CRUD, wire approval workflow (Temporal task queue), add domain reputation lookup cache, and schedule security sign-off. Assigned follow-ups to ENG-85480 (temporal workflow) and ENG-85481 (audit log schema change).
